item.title: Seeking Greenlight: Epstein didn't kill himself
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional): Modern events

+ show block
– hide block

Page Layout (Optional):

Special Containment Procedures: A copy of the scp is kept on hard drive kept in safe.

Description: Video is antimemetic. Foundation wants to know what happened in the video because Epstein was already on their radar for potential ties to a redacted GOI. Research with dangerous z-class mnestics was recently authorized

Document #XXXX-01: letter of authorization

Document #XXXX-02: Report on research with z class mnestics sent to O5. Contains test log with dialogue. Reveals that Epstein was murdered.

Document #XXXX-03: Internal document from O5 council. They believe that it was MC&D. Now they want to use that info to the advantage of the foundation.

Elevator Pitch: The surveillance feed of Epstein's death is anti-memetic. The SCP foundation wants to uncover the mystery of what happened as well as why it was covered up.

Central Narrative: Starting with the Description, I'm going to build a sense of an imposing conspiracy regarding Epstein's death. I will do this by hinting that Epstein was already on the Foundation's radar for being tied to a redacted GOI. I'm going to then hype up the efficacy of z-class mnestics by having their usage require authorization from the O5 council. Using Z-class mnestics as a benchmark, I'm gonna emphasize how extremely anti-memetic the footage. However, the testing will ultimately pull through and reveal that Epstein was murdered. Finally, in a post climax reveal, an internal document from the O5 council will reveal who they bbelieve murdered Epstein, tying back to the redacted GOI from earlier: Marshall, Carter, and Dark Ltd.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: This SCP focuses on modern conspiracies that I imagine everyone on the SCP wiki are familiar with (and maybe even buy into).

Additional Notes: I know that writing an article about Epstein requires care. If I make things to political, I can drive out half of the readers. I also have to make sure remain respectful to his victims. I'm aware of that responsibility and I won't post an article unless I'm confident that I satisfy both of those benchmarks.

item.title: Re: (Seeking Greenlight) Keep Him In The Dark
item.content:encoded:
I think the big thing that I didn't portray well enough in the original post, and will try to correct, is that the activation of the powers is almost completely unconscious and automatic. If he notices a change, he simply causes the change to no longer be there. The only way to stop it is for him to not notice changes, hence the constant monitoring and goal of keeping the various containments synced.

I agree that the narrative is a bit shallow and late. The new focus is much more on the foundation attempting to gaslight him so even if he does notice the changes, he thinks they're more in his own head, rather than reality being different. I also think the logs will be shorter and much more focused than I first intended. I've reworked the post to show the current idea for the chain of events, which should be a lot more definite and specific.

item.title: Re: Seeking Greenlight - Lavender
item.content:encoded:
Heyo Follow-up!

EXTRA SAND

+ show block
– hide block

The concept:

Elevator Pitch: A collection of objects with anomalous, antidepressive effects. These objects are (but not limited to): manifestation of feelings described as "relaxation, peacefulness, etc.", diminished symptoms in subjects diagnosed with major depressive dissorder, etc. Objects interact with each other and are essential between themselves (For example: Access to XXXX-2 can only be done by interacting with XXXX-1, XXXX-3 is stored inside of XXXX-2 and any sample taken will disappear when
exiting XXXX-2)

While there is more context here, the concept still comes across a bit flat as there isn't much to get invested in. Currently the skip still just feels like an antidepressant, with no major purpose or reason to really exist.- why and how will these objects be important? why should I as the reader care about it?

The narrative:

Central Narrative: Discovered in a lab of an unknown GoI. Consists of an air freshener, a room that can only be accessed by smelling the content of the air freshener, and a lavender plant contained inside the room. The objects manifest anomalous anti-depressive and anti-memetic properties, since subjects exposed to any of the XXXX objects will manifest a general feeling of well-being; but they won't remember any initial exposition. Audiovisual data stored in a digital medium will experience total corruption and will be intelligible, however, textual and analogue data storage doesn't seem to be affected.

Currently this is closer to additional info on the skip than a narrative, there isn't anything that really expands on the setup or shows what happens during the story. How does the Foundation find everything out? (assuming characters are included) how are they affected? What is everything building up to? whats the conflict? whats the main focus or theme?

The story still feels relatively unfinished as there isn't much to go off other than the setup. I'm not sure what direction the story will take, or how all of this will fit into a narrative. (from what I can see here (and the sandbox)) the narrative looks like it will be mostly based around the effects, which alone won't be able to carry the article as they don't offer much to the audience without any purpose or context.

Hook:

Hook/Attention-Grabber: There's a fourth object which is only known to high clearance ranks. It's a virus that is presumably the cause of major depressive disorder and it's linked to the human subconscious since unknown times. Cannot be cured with any current means and it's symptoms can only be diminished with antidepressants. Also, one of the three initial objects has a very high value to the Foundation; it's a Thaumiel, and has a very high possibility to counterattack XXXX-4. Linked to SCP-5000 narrative (or at least I tried)

The '4th object' still isn't really present in the concept or narrative, I'm not sure why its important or what role it plays. Along with this, I wouldn't recommend having the object cause an incurable depression, in the context of this it just feels like its being used as an effect.

-Quick second note, the skip should be able to stand on its own without needing to rely on other articles. I would highly recommend writing this as its own story as cross-linking can be quite hard to pull off.

Red or green?
Due to my afore mentioned concerns, no-greenlight.

- Overall the skip doesn't seem to have much behind the effects, which makes it feel a bit close to a "thing that does a thing".- whats the skips in-universe reason for existing? whats its purpose? how will all of this fit into a narrative?

-Some general advice on building narratives: try to get an idea of the beginning and the end, if you know what direction the narrative will take, then (generally speaking) it'll be easier to create.

If you would like me to give any further feedback, don't hesitate to send a PM, and if your looking for additional critiques or different perspectives, then I would highly recommend the butterfly squad. :)

cheers,

RED

Von Pincier's SCP-1548 left with him, but there remain numerous tales that refer to it, either directly as SCP-1548 or the Hateful Star. Others don't use either of these terms, but still make it relatively clear that this is the object in question. This goes to say that, despite the loss of the SCP itself, it or some similar entity still exists in the Foundationverse and is therefore possibly deserving of a character tag.

Articles:

  • Mystery Skipper Theater 3000 by RJB_R
  • A Place To Call Your Home by Billith
  • Incident 682-1548 by catboy637
  • CryogenChaos' Comment Tales and Tales of the Foundation Force Five by CryogenChaos

7 tales by 5 authors.

Less prominent mentions that might still count:

  • SCP-2117 by Ihp
  • Quiet Days by Dmatix
  • SCP-4568 by Logarithmika
  • SCP-5800 by not_a_seagull and MacWarren
  • Playing God by Rikks
  • SCP-3301 by djkaktus

Including these, it's 13 tales by 12 authors.

Note that this list does not include the new SCP-1548 by NatVoltaic, Varaxous's SCP-1548-EX, or djkaktus's SCP-4548, as they are clearly different entities from the original 1548.

item.title: Re: A World Of D-Class
item.content:encoded:
tldr; While it's an interesting idea, it feels like a cheat on a lot of levels and one that ignores a lot of narrative and in-universe issues. There are also some moral and logistical issues in-universe which need to be debated.

+ show block
– hide block

This is going to be a weird critique.

The basic problem is that D-class fulfills a necessary narrative function: Not only do they help demonstrate the inherent horror of the SCP Universe, but they also help to show that life in SCP-U is cheap and that a simple mistake can be fatal. While there is often a humor value in their deaths, it is a decidedly dark humor.

In short, the D-Class provide a necessary narrative element.

From an in-universe perspective, having a limited number of D-Class helps to ensure that the most sadistic of the Foundation researchers are forced to limit their activities, as well providing a reminder that if they get too sadistic they can become one of the victims. It also means that The Foundation must make the best use of a limited resource, adding an additional layer of realism in what is an otherwise unrealistic universe.

Eliminating the D-Class from the equation thus creates a number of issues as it eliminates a number of narrative elements, as well as a number of in-universe advantages. At the very least, it gives the most sadistic researcher the ability to ignore the Ethics Committee as well as eliminating any incentive for them to behave.

That said, this creates its own moral issues, as there are questions about using the dead for mere research. Not only would you need to show that the people are indeed evil, but that they deserved their fate. Also, some people would just feel uncomfortable using them as test subjects; the dead should remain so.

There's also the question of whether or not they are viable test subjects. While there are a number of situations where you want explorers, there are also a number of situations where you want living subjects, simply because they would react as living subjects (such as how chemicals affect them as well as the natural respiration systems).

In short, there's a lot of questions if they would be viable test subjects or not. And that ignores the number of SCPs where the containment protocols require living subjects.

While it's an interesting idea, I'm just not sure it would work with the SCP Universe.

item.title: Re: SCP-XXXX: The Sarkic Uprising of 1947
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hey there thesilentking. First off, allow me to apologise for the long delay in getting this review to you. Let’s take a look at your latest draft!

+ LBL
– hide block

Special Containment Procedures:

The start of this is incredibly messy and hard to follow. Consider colour-coding your text, especially if you’re using updates, which are usually in blue.

Also, you can start the updated conprocs on a new paragraph.

are to be detained and hand over

Keep your tenses consistent. “hand” -> “handed”.

with necessary alternations being made in accordance with standard containment of SK-BIO entities.

What does this mean? For a new reader, it doesn’t give me additional information that helps me understand the scip. Either specify what these “alternations” are or add a footnote to explain what “SK-BIO” refers to.

SCP-XXXX-1, 3, and 4 are only released from their containment units

This is already getting complicated. I’m generally not a fan of multiple instance-labelling, as it can get difficult for the reader to follow, fast. Generally, ask yourself if the payoff is worth it, and whether you can describe the entities without resorting to these labels, especially if they’re referring to an object with similar qualities.

NTS,1

Minor nitpick: your footnote should be before the comma, not after.

forfilling specific combat roles

Think you meant “fulfilling”.

In most respects SCP-XXXX-5 was a normal non-anomalous human.

Keep your tenses consistent. In the previous para, you were using “was” as “is”

SCP-XXXX-5 was located in a small wooden hut, guarded by SCP-XXXX-4.

See, this is confusing if we weren’t able to remember your labelling system. One option is to simply get rid of xxxx-5 label and mention the Karcist by name. OR convert his label to a PoI-designation, since he’s a separate humanoid entity.

To date, these have been the only SCP-XXXX entities to be recovered, though sightings of similar entities in the Bohemian and Bavarian Forests as well as in Central Italy have been reported. An investigation into a possible link between these entities and SCP-XXXX is currently ongoing.

This quite the hefty Description-segment. You’ve basically given away your entire narrative here, with testing logs, discovery logs and what I assume to be a final interview log with the Karcists all done and wrapped up.

One downside of this is you might tend to repeat all this later on in the article again, which is not productive. Usually, the Description segment is kept sparse, with the key details summarised and provided. Then, you’d go into detail in the latter addenda.

The following is a detailed timeline of events leading up to Incident XXXX-A & B

Notice I still don’t know what these two incidents are referring to. They’re briefly mentioned earlier in the article but you didn’t specify what they were.

The Sarkic cult which would go on to overtake Arlingpool, according to oral histories recovered from SCP-XXXX-5, originated from the Amur region of Siberia. Then known as the Church of Oastrikyo, they were hunted and driven away by Tsarist forces in 181█3, forcing them to flee to the coast.

Sorry, but what is this section supposed to be? Is it a log by the researcher? Uncovered documents? An interview with a Historian? I’m highly hesitant to read through a Wikipedia entry (basically an info-dump) as it’s likely to not contain any narrative or character development.

Below is an account from the diary of UIU Agent Daniel Blake5, from his first arrival at SCP-XXXX.

This is the first interesting part of the article, tbh. I always believe character should come first. Consider if you had simply moved this segment to the top of this section. Do you still need all that info when you can simply show what the town is like through the agent’s eyes.

The military's intervention eventually grew into a stalemate, with the SCP-XXXX inhabitants able to prevent significant military advances with the SK BIO organisms.

So I do like the fact you’ve interwoven historical events with the actions of the town and entities.

+ Overall
– hide block

(+/-) Overall, I’m torn. I do think the article picks up towards the end, but I’m still left wondering how the sarkic elements fit into this. It’s basically just producing monsters to fight in wars, yes? Eventually, this leads to conflict with the government (but not the Foundation?) I feel that the concept has potential, but your sarkic elements need to be emphasised a little more to really drive home the horror aspect.

(-) Structure and execution are where I’m struggling: the entire article reads like a history lesson, which keeps its clinical tone but lacks any tension-building or narrative stakes. You’re basically retelling the events in a discovery log, and by the end of the article, it’s just an “okay, that’s cool. So what?” kinda feeling. It doesn’t help that the Karcist dies at the very beginning of the article, so we kinda already know that the Foundation has prevailed.

You’d need to majorly restructure this, however, so that it’s more in line with a traditional narrative. If you’re playing with sarkicism, it’s essential to keep some of the mystery alive as we progress through the article. Make us wonder what’s going on instead of just telling us the facts from the start. Have the Foundation investigate the claims and forget the US government, I feel.

Overall, I would no-vote this in its current state.

If you decide to revise the draft / respond below, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to take another look. For now, all the best with the writing!

item.title: Re: Tale critique: Stop Right There
item.content:encoded:
Summoned via PM:

Hey there Jarvis122. First off, allow me to apologise for the long delay in getting this review to you. Let’s take a look at your latest draft!

+ LBL
– hide block

You have accessed the Foundation’s Level 4 file network.

I’m not sure why this is coloured in blue? Usually, blue is used only to highlight updates to an article.

Input: * * * * *

At first glance, I wasn’t sure what I was reading. Maybe you can make it clearer that we’re looking at a computer terminal screen. This could be “Input Password:” for example.

I heard this particular incident stirred quite a ruckus for the Foundation.

This line is severely out of place in terms of tone. Notice how the previous lines adopt a formal, clinical tone of a computer’s voice. Suddenly, this line appears with an opinion. Unless this serves a purpose later in the article, I would rephrase/cut this.

arrive at a secluded car park 20 meters away from Sally’s Catalogue of Pages

Keep your tenses consistent. In the following sentence, you swap to past tense. “arrive” -> “arrived” then.

Matthew Pickett spotted them and questioned them.

Remove redundant words. Here, “them” is repeated twice, in close proximity. Get rid of the first one.

The two men intended to enter the store and claim it

What does “claim it” mean? That’s an odd choice of words. Did you mean “rob” it?

No wallet was reported by staff

Ah. You see how it wasn’t clear the store was a lost-and-found office from the start?

PoI-5641 distanced himself from the officers

What does this mean? If he ran, just say he ran.

The man continued to claim innocence

Which man?

what he claimed to be an illegal arrest, backing towards his vehicle.

My impressions of this initial log aren’t positive. It’s overly detailed and the format doesn’t suit that of a Tale. The freedom of the formatting means you’re allowed to write scenes of dialogue using regular prose. Instead, you’ve chosen to write in the style of a traditional log in an scp article. Consider how this scene and the tension would have been elevated so much more if you had written this as an actual video/audio recording.

Officer Pickett then struck the PoI repeatedly.

Why did this happen? Police officers don’t (usually initiate violence unless they feel their lives are being threatened.

Aftermath: PoI-5641 and PoI-5642 were detained by Springfield Police and are being held in Springfield Municipal Jail.

Notice how by the end of this first entry, I still don’t know what’s anomalous about both PoIs or the GoI they belong to. This is a serious error. You only have the first page to hook a reader’s attention, and you’ve wasted it by just portraying a regular robbery and arrest. Unless I missed something, I don’t see any anomalous effects or reasons for the Foundation to get involved.

— Geoffrey Barraclough, Site-681 Director

Ah? So the Foundation raided and took over the base? I must have missed that beat.

The five items that were being transferred to this site

What five items?

though their definition of anomalous isn’t as…developed as what the Foundation handles with

Again, this makes me question the Foundation’s involvement at this point. I think you need to highlight the stakes / danger of the scp or GoI MUCH earlier.

he made a post listing Site-681 as a location of interest.

This shouldn’t be sufficient grounds for investigation. What you’re suggesting is that the Foundation investigates internet conspiracy theories and raids them based on unsubstantiated info. Perhaps tell us why it’s a location of interest from the start? Give us anomalous sightings (whether fabricated or not).

Freyberg: Any information we find needs to be given to the investigation committee, which you already told us is being organized by the O5s.

Unclear what this last section of the log is meant to convey. You’re firing off names and connections and bureaucracy quite rapidly, and it’s hard to keep up. I’d highly recommend trimming this portion, especially if it isn’t relevant to the story.

Input: Investigation Committee Operation Log-06

This entire log is unnecessary as it’s repeated information from the previous one. You’ve already mentioned the PoI to be captured. Keep either one but not both.

+ Overall
– hide block

Because they were investigating 2230 9th Street. The 2330 on the post was a typo.

I’m really torn on this. I know I was one of the reviewers who gave you the initial greenlight, but perhaps I should have asked you to clarify the format in which you’d be writing in. A lot of the initial beats and tension you were aiming for (mass conspiracy, the head researcher’s ambition for a promotion, a possible mole in the Foundation) did not come through during this Tale. Instead, it read mostly like a series of logs in every other scp article, just that in this case, it wasn’t clear what the anomaly was, why it was dangerous to begin with, and basically, what the whole fuss was about.

There seems to be some goal of the PoI to uncover secrecy and promote transparency, but it’s muddled throughout the logs, and only mentioned in one or two lines throughout. A lot of your detail could be cut, for example, and the bare-bones story would still be there.

Personally, I would no-vote this in its current state. I feel you need to make the anomaly much clearer at the beginning, as well as highlight the intentions and goals of the main character (which I’d advised you before). Right now, there are too many people running around, the O5 council getting involved for no reason, and the GoI coming across as trolls on the forum. I would suggest cutting characters that serve little purpose, and to reemphasise what their goals are from the beginning – for example, do you really need:

Frederic Pittman, O5 Council Representative, Kendall Callaghan, Ethics Committee Representative, Conan Freyberg, Head of Investigation Committee-9182 and Alexander Bradford, Head of Committee Operations

Lastly, do consider revamping this to a proper Tale format, which means majority of the article should be written in regular prose. There still could be logs here and there, but don’t forget: a Tale should be a short story. I should be able to hear your voice as the author throughout. At least, that’s my definition of it. Of course, feel free to look for other reviewers to get second opinions.

If you decide to revise the draft, do drop me another PM and I’ll do my best to respond again. All the best with the writing for now!

item.title: Re: Amateur wizards and how to contain them
item.content:encoded:
Responding to request via PM:

+ show block
– hide block

I will admit, I think the elevator pitch has some charm to it, and based on that summary think your idea certainly has potential.

not only does the article highlight the foundations struggle to contain an scp that has a hard time performing even the most minor tasks without getting magic involved, failing at said magic and accidentally bringing down the nearest wall on top of him (when he was trying to make his bed make itself). while still staying kosher with the ethics department.

See, this is where you begin to lose me. If this kid is such a liability when he is awake, why does the Foundation not put him into a medically induced coma, and wake him up when needed. There is certainly precedent for that in articles across the wiki, and given the alternative is the kid bringing down walls trying to make his bed it's hard for you to really justify the Foundation just letting him hang in a standard containment cell. It's one thing if you have the Foundation getting bamboozled while acting in a competent manner, but a huge turn-off for me as a reader if you portray them acting like idiots to highlight how cool your skip is.

The scp’s complete immaturity and lack of expertise or knowledge of just how powerful he can be, make him extremely hard to utilize in any situation.

More reason to just slap him into a coma and raise him when needed. The Foundation should not suffer fools gladly.

I am extremely worried about this scp being to overpowered or lacking in restriction.

Then add restrictions. Show that the Foundation is not just catering to a teenager to keep on its good side.

All in all you have a solid premise, but your execution leaves much to be desired. Have the Foundation step up and not handle something this dangerous with kids gloves and you'll be in a much better space.

Best of luck.

Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Elevator Pitch: A portal to a hell of sorts that contains all evil people that have died, which the Foundation decides to use for D-Class

Hook/Attention-Grabber: It gives a reasonable method of providing a major part of the Foundation's required human cost.

Additional follow-up, per PM request:

+ show block
– hide block

The anomaly is located within Bryce Canyon National Park, where a dimension (at a certain time of night) anomalously takes the place of the park.

Christ alive, how on Earth do you hide an entire National Park sized area going missing at the same time every night. You're going to need to really knock the containment procedures out of the park to handwave that.

and individuals who have died and do not profess to any religion or cult.

How do they know these are people who have died?

After a D-Class was able to return with her daughter however, research is strangely ramped up by Harry, as he becomes more and more unprofessional.

Did the D-Class just stumble across her daughter, or was that the mission? Also, does no one attempt to stop the D-class from just leaving with another's soul?

The MTF is picked off as the soldiers are taken to different caverns by the demons.

Why though, the MTF members are not dead.

but Harry is the last one remaining in the group.

Why is Harry, the one who seems like they would least be capable of self-defense compared to trained MTF soldiers, the last one left?

For a Foundation rendition of the Orpheus myth, I can think you are starting to get on to the right track. You have a few more plot holes I would like to see hammered out before I would like to give my Greenlight, but the above is a vast improvement over the first few renditions.

item.title: Re: [LOOKING FOR GREENLIGHT] An SCP Music Stand (Not a Jojo Reference)
item.content:encoded:
Directed here by PM:

+ show block
– hide block

Enough instruments playing the song on it manifest entities that appear to reenact actions based on the song being played, though if it’s played near a stage the effects are focused onto the stage, showing the actual events in question reenacted.

How close to the stage does this need to be? Additionally, how do they know there are events being portrayed by the music? If I just typed a random mix of letters onto a piece of paper and placed it on the anomaly, and had the music directed to a stage, what kind of events would this be?

Depending on the song the events range from benign to XK Class to a local area if uncontained.

Yeah, see, the thing with XK class events is if they happen there isn't really bouncing back from that, so you might need to tone down the power here a smidge, or at least have it presumed.

Watching too many of these turn certain people into cult-like groupie's that can make destructible but anomalous duplicates through unknown means.

So… a compulsion effect? Doesn't that seem a bit cliche?

With respect to the central narrative, you seem to focus more on Ixmer, almost to the point where I have to wonder what's the point of having the music stand item associated with this, since it seems like you have a lot more you care to write about this entity.

An SCP file left on it by accident reveals a major connection with one to The Factory, showing the entity using assets to buy out the Foundation.

That comes across as a very shoe-horned way of getting the Factory involved in this skip. While you obviously can include what ever GoI you want, this reads like you are including the Factory for the sake of including the Factory.

All in all, you have a lot of moving parts to this skip, but none of them really congeal together. I'd argue focusing on Ixmer would be the strongest move, as the rest of the pieces you include here seem more like after thought in comparison, and I only imagine would bog the piece as a whole down.

item.title: Re: The Painter (Old Concept)
item.content:encoded:
[Placeholder]

When humanising someone, you don't make them even more weird by adding negative effects like literally bleeding whenever the painter finishes a painting. It just ostracises them further from being human, you know? It's just sort of like, artificially placed in to make readers feel sympathy because you couldn't think of a more believable detriment. I think that portion could use some more work - try reflecting on yourself, when you see people, what is the thing you find yourself pitying them for?

As for a backstory

But then who afflicted this curse on him, for what reason? Because yes, it is a gruesome fate but what did he do wrong in the first place to be condemned to it? I fear if you go down this path it might lead to your plot becoming too dense/convoluted as you introduce gods and spirits hexing him, so I'm going to say right now to change your focus up a bit.

Focus on the character development of the old painter instead. What is his emotional development as the story progresses? Is there a point of catharsis or realisation that really tugs at the heartstrings of readers? Is there some kind of side character that can guide him to that conclusion?
